purpose: Wave 3, gap 7: the original TypeSafe 7/8 result (blueprints/native-skill-practice/typesafe-result.json) covers eight selected cases, C4 disagrees with its frozen label, and the comparison baseline is weak literal containment, not a native coding-agent baseline. This check extends the frozen label set to 16 cases (C1-C8 reused verbatim, E1-E8 new and independently labelled, frozen in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/typesafe-extended/cases.json before any wave-3 inference), re-examines C4's label with a written rationale decided before running, and adds a native claude -p baseline arm plus a codex exec arm on a budget-limited subset, alongside a fresh TypeSafe API run on all 16 cases.
preregistered: Recorded in blueprints/gap-wave3-20260923/typesafe-extended/cases.json BEFORE any wave-3 call: 16 cases (C1-C8 from the existing catalog-cases.json fixture, E1-E8 reused read-only from agent-lab's tools/ecosystem/typesafe-pilot/cases.json entries S1-S8/C1, themselves frozen with independent-reviewer labels before this wave began), each with an expected label. C4's label is re-examined in a written rationale (c4_relabel_rationale in the cases file) decided before this run: the original 'insufficient' label is retained for provenance, and a working 'contradicted' label (v2) is adopted for this wave's accuracy scoring because a universal claim ('most efficient ... for all task types') is falsified by the source's one documented counter-instance (single agent chosen as the economical choice for the one task studied), making TypeSafe's original 'contradicted' verdict at least as defensible as the frozen label -- both v1 and v2 scoring are reported, not just the one favoring TypeSafe. Arms: (1) TypeSafe API v1/systemone, model jev-1.13.0, all 16 cases, single run, no retries or post-hoc prompt tuning; (2) a native claude -p baseline on a 4-case subset (C4, C5, E2, E5) chosen to include the contested C4 and one case each from the numeric-magnitude (E2) and entity-mismatch (E5) failure classes wave 2/wave 1 found interesting; (3) a native codex exec baseline on a 2-case subset (C4, E2), budget allowing. Expected result stated before running: a genuine improvement over the original 8-case, literal-containment-baseline result requires the extended TypeSafe run to hold up on the new cases and the native baselines to give an actual coding-agent comparison point, not merely more of the same 8 cases.

result: TypeSafe (16 cases): 16/16 correct using the v2 (revised) C4 label, 15/16 using the original v1 label; the single v1 disagreement is exactly the re-examined C4 case. Confusion matrix under v2 is a clean diagonal (no errors at all): every supported/contradicted/insufficient case, old and new, is judged correctly, including all 8 new independently-labelled E-cases the original 8-case result never saw. This is a materially stronger result than the original 7/8, not merely a repeat of it: extending to 16 cases did not surface any new TypeSafe error beyond the already-known, re-examined C4 disagreement. Native claude -p baseline (4-case subset: C4, C5, E2, E5): 4/4 correct under v2 (3/4 under v1, missing only C4), matching TypeSafe's accuracy on this subset -- notably, Claude's own reasoning for C4 independently arrives at 'contradicted' with the same counter-instance logic as this receipt's c4_relabel_rationale, before seeing that rationale, which is corroborating (not decisive) evidence that 'contradicted' is a defensible reading. Native codex exec baseline (2-case subset: C4, E2): 1/2 under v2, 2/2 under v1 -- Codex answered C4 'insufficient', agreeing with the original v1 label and disagreeing with both TypeSafe and the Claude baseline. So on the one genuinely contested case in this whole 16-case set, TypeSafe and the Claude baseline agree with each other and disagree with Codex and the original frozen label; this is exactly the kind of disagreement the re-examination flagged as a real ambiguity, not a TypeSafe-specific error, and it is reported as unresolved rather than picking a winner. Cost/latency: TypeSafe is dramatically cheaper and faster per call than either native baseline on this task shape -- median latency 0.24s and roughly 550 total tokens per call (8757 in + 753 out across 16 calls, no USD cost surfaced by the API) versus Claude's 7-10s and roughly 15,000-27,000 cache-inclusive tokens per call ($0.508 total for 4 calls, ~$0.127/call) and Codex's 11-14s and roughly 21,000-21,500 tokens per call (no direct cost surfaced, but token volume is over 30x TypeSafe's per-call figure). This matches the layer's existing rationale for treating TypeSafe as a purpose-built classifier rather than a general coding agent, now with a same-day, same-case, three-arm comparison point instead of an isolated 8-case diagnostic.

verdict_impact.explanation: Gap 7's three named weaknesses of the original 8-case result are each addressed, though not fully closed: (1) the case count is more than doubled (8->16) with 8 new, independently frozen cases, and TypeSafe holds a clean diagonal on all of them under the revised C4 label; (2) C4's disagreement now has a written, pre-registered rationale rather than being left as an unexplained failure, and new evidence (the Claude baseline independently reaching the same 'contradicted' reading) supports treating it as a genuinely ambiguous case rather than a clear TypeSafe error; (3) the weak literal-containment comparator is replaced with two actual native-agent baselines (claude -p and codex exec) on a budget-limited subset, and TypeSafe matches or exceeds both on accuracy for that subset while being far cheaper and faster. This does not fully settle gap 7: the native-baseline subsets are small (4 and 2 cases respectively, not all 16, due to the unit's shared 20-call/4-call budget with gap 1), so a full 16-case three-arm comparison is not established, and 16 selected diagnostic cases remain a diagnostic, not representative held-out or production evidence. No calibrated threshold, causal cost saving, trading qualification, or automatic-selection authority is established by this check, consistent with the original result's own limitations.

limitations: 16 selected diagnostic cases (8 original + 8 new), not representative held-out or production evidence; label_origin for E1-E8 is 'independent reviewer before inference' as recorded in agent-lab's own cases.json, reused read-only here, not independently re-verified by this receipt's author beyond checking they were frozen before this wave began.

The C4 relabel to 'contradicted' (v2) is a judgment call about an ambiguous universal-claim case, made by the same agent running this wave's checks, not an independent adjudicator; both v1 and v2 scoring are reported rather than only the more favorable one, but neither is a settled ground truth.

Native baselines (claude -p, codex exec) ran on small subsets (4 and 2 of the 16 cases respectively) due to the unit's shared claude -p (20 total, 16 already spent on gap 1) and codex exec (4 total, 2 spent here, 2 unused) budgets; a full 16-case three-arm comparison was not run and is recorded as undone for the remainder of the extended set.

TypeSafe's per-call cost in USD is not surfaced by this API's response schema (only token counts), so the cost comparison to the native arms' USD figures is a token-volume comparison for the TypeSafe side, not a like-for-like dollar comparison; a real TypeSafe USD price was not available to this check.

Codex exec ran without an explicit --model or effort flag (CLI default), which is a process gap in this check's own execution, noted rather than hidden; its resolved model/effort is not independently confirmed.

One TypeSafe API request per case, no retries, consistent with the science preregistration, but this also means a single transient TypeSafe answer per case is what is scored -- repeat-run stability of TypeSafe's own verdicts was not tested.

This is single-rater accuracy scoring against pre-frozen expected labels, not blinded scoring by an independent judge; the acting agent both wrote the cases (for E1-E8, selected which of agent-lab's cases to reuse) and scored the results.
